headline.headline: HAWKS CLAW PAST MAGIC IN OVERTIME THRILLER TO SEIZE SERIES EDGE
headline.deck: Atlanta survives Orlando scare, 132-125, as conference semifinals heat up
headline.body:
ORLANDO — The Atlanta Hawks refused to fold Wednesday night, grinding past the Orlando Magic 132-125 in a playoff game that stretched every nerve inside Kia Center. The road win gives Atlanta a commanding foothold in the Eastern Conference semifinals, as the Hawks proved capable of winning in hostile territory against a Magic squad that would not go quietly.

Orlando pushed Atlanta to the limit, trimming deficits and forcing the Hawks to answer every run. The Magic's young core generated 125 points, a total that would win most regular-season games, but Atlanta's firepower proved deeper and more relentless. The Hawks' backcourt refused to let Orlando seize momentum for any sustained stretch, and when the Magic drew close, Atlanta responded with buckets that kept the lead comfortable enough to protect.

Elsewhere in the Eastern Conference on Wednesday, the Washington Wizards handed the Milwaukee Bucks a 128-116 defeat at Capital One Arena, a result that continued to scramble expectations in a bracket full of surprises. The Wizards' home floor proved a genuine advantage, and Milwaukee's inability to slow Washington's offense raised serious questions about the Bucks heading into the next game of the series.

secondary.headline: TIMBERWOLVES OPEN WITH A STATEMENT, PUNISH HEAT BY 25
secondary.deck: Minnesota dominates Miami 131-106 to begin second-round series with authority
secondary.body:
MIAMI — The Minnesota Timberwolves arrived in South Florida on Wednesday night and left little doubt about their intentions, dismantling the Miami Heat 131-106 in Game 1 of their Eastern Conference semifinals series. The 25-point margin was not flattering to a Heat franchise that has built its identity on playoff toughness and late-game resilience.

Minnesota controlled the game from end to end, pushing the pace and burying Miami under a relentless offensive attack that the Heat had no answer for. The Timberwolves' defense smothered Miami's transition opportunities and turned the contest into a wire-to-wire exercise in dominance. Game 2 of the series remains on the horizon, but Wednesday's performance sent an unmistakable message to every team still standing in the bracket.

secondary.headline: CELEBRINI SPARKS SHARKS, SENATORS RETURN STIRS TKACHUK DRAMA
secondary.deck: San Jose's rookie phenom fuels Ottawa showdown as Brady Tkachuk faces former fans
secondary.body:
OTTAWA — Macklin Celebrini carried a two-goal performance into Thursday's matchup between the San Jose Sharks and the Ottawa Senators, setting the stage for one of the more emotionally charged games of the second round. The Senators enter at 7-3 in the Atlantic Division, a team playing with confidence at home, where a particularly raucous reception awaits a familiar face: Brady Tkachuk, whose return to Ottawa has already been compared to some of the most uncomfortable homecomings in North American sports history.

Tkachuk, who built his identity and fan base in Ottawa before departing, can expect a sustained chorus of boos from a crowd with long memories. The dynamic adds a theatrical layer to what is already a legitimate hockey game between a Sharks team riding Celebrini's momentum and a Senators squad that has been one of the pleasant surprises of the postseason. How Tkachuk responds to the hostile atmosphere could define the tone of the entire series.

secondary.headline: ATHLETICS HAND BASEBALL OPERATIONS TO 31-YEAR-OLD TAYLOR SMITH
secondary.deck: Owner John Fisher bets on youth to reshape a franchise still searching for identity
secondary.body:
The Oakland Athletics made a decision Wednesday that will either look visionary or reckless in five years, hiring 31-year-old Taylor Smith as president of baseball operations. Owner John Fisher justified the move with a phrase that will follow this franchise for as long as Smith holds the job: "The world is run by 31-year-olds today." Whether that philosophy translates to a winning roster remains the central question hanging over a ballclub that has endured years of upheaval.

Smith becomes one of the youngest executives to hold a top baseball operations title for a major league franchise, and the hire signals that Fisher intends to rebuild around analytics and youth rather than established baseball names. The Athletics, still navigating a complicated period in their franchise history, will now lean on a 31-year-old to make the decisions that determine whether the organization can compete. The baseball world will be watching to see if Fisher's instinct was bold or simply impulsive.

column.headline: THE WIZARDS BEATING MILWAUKEE IS THE STORY NOBODY WANTS TO ADMIT IS REAL
column.body:
Washington beating Milwaukee 128-116 on Wednesday should not be dismissed as a fluke or a bad night for the Bucks. It should be read as what it increasingly appears to be: a team that has figured something out in the postseason, at home, with a crowd that has rediscovered why it shows up. The Wizards are not supposed to be here. They are here anyway, and they are winning in a way that does not look accidental.

Milwaukee has the names and the pedigree, but names do not guard the paint and pedigree does not make open threes. If the Bucks cannot solve Washington's home court in the next game, this series will become a full-blown crisis for a franchise that has been circling that word for two playoff runs now. Give the Wizards credit. Stop treating their wins as a surprise and start treating them as evidence.

story.headline: OHTANI CLEARS MEDICAL HURDLE, SETS SIGHTS ON MOUND IN 2027
story.deck: Dodgers superstar avoids surgery, giving Los Angeles hope for full pitching return next season.
story.body:
Shohei Ohtani will not go under the knife. The Los Angeles Dodgers announced Thursday that their transcendent two-way star requires no surgical procedure to address the ailments that sidelined his pitching in 2026, a revelation that sent a jolt of optimism through Chavez Ravine and rattled every front office in the National League. Club president of baseball operations Andrew Friedman confirmed Ohtani is expected to return to the pitching mound in 2027, setting the stage for what could be the most anticipated comeback in the sport since Tommy John surgery became a household phrase.

Ohtani, who captured the baseball world's imagination with his historic 50-home-run, 50-stolen-base campaign in 2024 before undergoing Tommy John surgery, spent the 2026 season focused exclusively on his designated hitter duties while his reconstructed elbow continued its long road back. The news that no further procedure is necessary represents a clean bill of health that the Dodgers had privately hoped for but dared not guarantee publicly. Los Angeles remained a postseason force during his pitching absence, but the prospect of a fully operational Ohtani on the bump transforms the franchise from dangerous to historically formidable.

Around the rest of the league, the offseason machinery ground forward on multiple fronts. In Oakland, Athletics owner John Fisher raised eyebrows by installing 31-year-old Taylor Smith as president of baseball operations, declaring with characteristic bluntness that the world is run by 31-year-olds today. In the Bronx, Yankees manager Aaron Boone pushed back against calls for a harder clubhouse hand, insisting the culture inside New York's locker room remains a strength despite a postseason exit that left fans and analysts demanding accountability. The hot stove is burning early this October.

story.headline: TIMBERWOLVES STEAMROLL HEAT IN DOMINANT SEASON OPENER
story.deck: Minnesota rolls into Miami and wins going away, 131-106, behind a suffocating team effort.
story.body:
MIAMI -- The Minnesota Timberwolves served notice to the Eastern Conference on Wednesday night, dismantling the Miami Heat 131-106 in a game that was never as close as the final score suggested. Minnesota controlled the contest from wire to wire, piling up points against a Heat squad that had no answer for the Timberwolves' attack in what amounted to a 25-point blowout on Miami's home floor.

The result moved Minnesota to 1-0 and put the league on notice that the Timberwolves are bringing the same suffocating, high-powered brand of basketball that carried them deep into the postseason a year ago. Miami, meanwhile, fell to 0-1 and faces immediate questions about its ability to compete with the conference's upper tier after being handled so thoroughly on opening night.

Elsewhere around the league Wednesday, Atlanta's Hawks topped Orlando 132-125 in a competitive road win at the Kia Center, the Washington Wizards stunned Milwaukee 128-116 at home, and the Charlotte Hornets quieted Brooklyn 110-103 on the road. The Hawks and Hornets both moved to 1-0, setting up a compelling Eastern Conference clash Thursday night in Atlanta.

story.headline: CIRELLI, LIGHTNING CARRY MOMENTUM INTO DENVER SHOWDOWN
story.deck: Tampa Bay rides Anthony Cirelli's two-goal surge into a clash with Colorado.
story.body:
The Tampa Bay Lightning arrive in Denver on Thursday riding one of the Eastern Conference's hottest starts, carrying a 7-2 record and the momentum of Anthony Cirelli's two-goal performance into a marquee matchup against the Colorado Avalanche at Ball Arena. Cirelli's recent outburst has sharpened Tampa Bay's attack at precisely the right moment, as the Lightning look to press their advantage atop the Atlantic Division standings.

Colorado enters the game at 5-4-1, a record that reflects an inconsistent early season for a club that expected to contend deep into spring. The Avalanche will need a strong collective effort to slow a Lightning squad that has allowed few openings through nine games and continues to deploy one of the league's most structured defensive systems alongside its high-powered forwards.

Elsewhere around the league Thursday, the Pittsburgh Penguins, mired at 3-6-1, welcome the Florida Panthers in a matchup that pits Pittsburgh's struggling offense against a Panthers team sitting at 5-3-2 in the Atlantic. In the Pacific, Macklin Celebrini and the San Jose Sharks, buoyed by the young center's two-goal effort, visit the Ottawa Senators, who own the Atlantic's second-best record at 7-3. Chicago also hosts Montreal in a non-conference battle at the United Center.

story.headline: QUARTERBACK CAROUSEL SPINS WILDLY AS TEAMS REMAKE ROSTERS FOR 2026
story.deck: Several franchises are betting big on new signal-callers this spring.
story.body:
The NFL offseason has become a quarterback marketplace unlike any seen in recent memory, with at least five franchises overhauling their most important position since the confetti settled on Super Bowl LX in February. The Las Vegas Raiders moved aggressively last month, shipping three draft picks to the Carolina Panthers for disgruntled starter Bryce Young, who struggled through two brutal seasons in Charlotte and is now viewed as a reclamation project under new Raiders offensive coordinator Greg Roman. Meanwhile, the New Orleans Saints finalized a three-year, $112 million deal with free agent veteran Kirk Cousins, betting that a change of scenery from Atlanta can resurrect the 38-year-old's career alongside a rebuilt offensive line.

The NFL Draft in late April added more fuel to the reshuffling. The Cleveland Browns, picking second overall after another disappointing campaign, selected Colorado quarterback Shedeur Sanders, ending months of speculation about the franchise's long-term direction. Browns general manager Andrew Berry called Sanders the most pro-ready passer in the class, pointing to his pocket composure and completion percentage above 72 percent in his final college season. The Tennessee Titans, drafting fourth, pivoted to Miami's Cam Ward, giving the franchise its third first-round quarterback in seven years.

Beyond the quarterback frenzy, the open market has reshaped defenses across the league. The Philadelphia Eagles retained linebacker Zack Baun on a richly deserved four-year extension after his breakout 2025 campaign, while the Dallas Cowboys, still rebuilding trust with their fanbase, added cornerback Tre'Davious White on a one-year prove-it deal worth $9 million. Several teams open training camp in late July with more questions than answers, setting the stage for what promises to be one of the more unpredictable regular seasons in recent memory.
